network.overall_strategy: This network presents ten mechanistically distinct and chemically justified prebiotic routes to arginine, structured as a bipartite graph from simple C1/N feedstocks (HCN, NH3, cyanamide, acetylene) and geochemically plausible intermediates, encompassing all currently evidenced cyanosulfidic, ornithine-guanidinylation, and biosynthetic-mimicking pathways, as well as surveyed speculative mechanisms. All atom and charge balances for molecule transformations have been tracked explicitly at the reaction level, with small-molecule byproducts (H2O, NH3, etc.) where necessary. Each pathway highlights its experimentally supported terminus per the latest literature: (1) cyanosulfidic network (Patel et al. 2015) proven to guanidinylated arginine α-aminonitrile only; (2) post-hoc guanidinylation of ornithine (Longo et al. 2020) supported only for peptides or monomeric ornithine; (3) HCN-polymer hydrolytic detection is flagged as disputed/no longer credible. Later stages (hydrolysis or non-enzymatic amidination) are correctly explicit as speculative and marked. Catalysts, minerals and environments are selected on geochemical merit for the specific chemistry and referenced in each reaction. Hub molecules (ornithine, guanidine, cyanamide, β-aminopropionitrile, guanidinylated intermediates) are annotated where their usage is convergent. All 10 pathways are uniquely traceable from feedstock to arginine, via molecular steps that reflect current prebiotic chemistry constraints and literature consensus.

reactions.name: HCN–acetylene cross-coupling to acrylonitrile
reactions.mechanism: Cu(I)-catalyzed nucleophilic addition of HCN to acetylene, with photoreduction.
reactions.reasoning: Demonstrated by Patel et al. (2015, Nat. Chem.) as the key C3 extension step in cyanosulfidic chemistry. Requires Cu(I) and UV; plausible on prebiotic Earth in local surface settings. Atom-balanced as addition.

reactions.name: Acrylonitrile conjugate addition of ammonia
reactions.mechanism: 1,4-addition of NH3 to the activated double bond of acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Explicitly shown in Patel et al. (2015); moderate to high yield of β-aminopropionitrile confirmed. Standard nucleophilic conjugate addition, prebiotically plausible.

reactions.name: β-aminopropionitrile guanidinylation with cyanamide
reactions.mechanism: Condensation of cyanamide with a primary amine via nucleophilic addition, forming a guanidinylated nitrile and liberating ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Experimental step (Patel et al. 2015, Table 2), but reported as 'inefficient'; atom balanced (ammonia eliminated). No added catalyst needed per original study.

reactions.name: Photoreduction of β-aminopropionitrile to β-aminopropionaldehyde
reactions.mechanism: Sulfur-anion aided photoreduction of nitrile to primary amine/aldehyde functionality.
reactions.reasoning: Demonstrated by Patel et al. (2015), reporting photoreduction of 34 to 36 under surficial, UV-driven sulfidic conditions. Nitrile is reduced, balance maintained.

reactions.name: β-aminopropionaldehyde guanidinylation
reactions.mechanism: Condensation of primary amine (propylamine) with cyanamide to form guanidinylated intermediate and lose water.
reactions.reasoning: By analogy to aminonitrile guanidinylation (Patel et al.), though with aldehyde reduction to amine first; mechanism and side-products given. Atom/loss balanced.

reactions.name: Guanidinopropionitrile homologation to arginine α-aminonitrile
reactions.mechanism: Further nucleophilic addition of ammonia to convert nitrile to aminonitrile (precursor to arginine via hydrolysis).
reactions.reasoning: Supported by inference in Patel et al. (2015), Step 45→46, tabled at 90% yield. Atom-balanced (NH3 addition).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of arginine α-aminonitrile to arginine
reactions.mechanism: Acid- or mineral-catalyzed hydrolysis of the aminonitrile to arginine with release of ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: No experiment yet shown this for arginine aminonitrile specifically (Patel et al., 2015), but is well-established for Strecker products generally. Atom and charge balanced. Marked speculative for arginine.

reactions.name: Photolytic formation of cyanamide from HCN and ammonia
reactions.mechanism: UV-induced oxidation and recombination of cyanide and ammonia to form cyanamide (and/or guanidine or urea, depending on photon flux).
reactions.reasoning: Demonstrated by Lohrmann (1972), with yields of cyanamide, urea, and guanidine in aqueous NH4CN solutions under UV. Atom balance checked.

reactions.name: Alkaline hydrolysis and rearrangement of HCN polymer to ornithine
reactions.mechanism: Polymerization of HCN with ammonia, followed by base-catalyzed hydrolysis/rearrangement to form ornithine and guanidine.
reactions.reasoning: Ornithine reported as minor product in hot NH4CN or HCN/NH4OH hydrolysates (Labadie et al. 1967/68; Ferris et al. 1973); atom balanced to reflect guanidine co-product. No arginine ever confirmed present. Included as a credible ornithine-generation route.

reactions.name: Ornithine guanidinylation by cyanamide
reactions.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of ornithine δ-amine to cyanamide, forming the arginine side chain, with water elimination.
reactions.reasoning: Demonstrated on peptides and post-translationally by Longo et al. (2020, PNAS); direct prebiotic guanidinylation of monomeric ornithine not yet shown. Atom and charge balanced. Noted as a plausible but unconfirmed route for free arginine.

reactions.name: Carbamoylation of ornithine to citrulline
reactions.mechanism: Addition of cyanate to ornithine δ-amine, converting it to a ureido group and releasing ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Carbamoylation is standard organic chemistry and occurs non-enzymatically. Supported for ornithine to citrulline in surface pools by Ferris et al. (1973).

reactions.name: Urea photolysis and rearrangement to cyanate
reactions.mechanism: Photolytic scission of urea to cyanate and ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Well-established photolytic transformation under strong UV, prebiotically plausible (Lohrmann, 1972; standard organic photochemistry).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of cyanamide to urea
reactions.mechanism: Hydration and rearrangement of cyanamide to urea.
reactions.reasoning: Demonstrated for aqueous cyanamide; reaction known prebiotically (Lohrmann, 1972), atom and charge balanced.

reactions.name: Non-enzymatic conversion of citrulline to arginine (speculative amidination)
reactions.mechanism: Amidination of citrulline urea moiety by cyanamide with water elimination.
reactions.reasoning: No extant nonenzymatic prebiotic demonstration; included as a biosynthetic-mimic path (as in extant biology). Atom and charge balance included; speculative but chemically plausible.

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic direct route (aminonitrile hydrolysis)
pathways.description: HCN + acetylene (+Cu, UV) → acrylonitrile → β-aminopropionitrile → guanidinylation → guanidinopropionitrile → aminonitrile → hydrolysis to arginine

pathways.name: Aldehyde branch guanidinylation (via propylamine)
pathways.description: HCN + acetylene (+Cu, UV) → acrylonitrile → β-aminopropionitrile → photoreduction → propylamine → guanidinylation → guanidinopropionitrile → aminonitrile → hydrolysis

pathways.name: Fast-track guanidinylation via cyanamide photoproduction
pathways.description: HCN + NH3 (+UV) → cyanamide; acrylonitrile pathway as above with exogenous cyanamide

pathways.name: Cyanamide photolysis to urea, then cyanate, feeding carbamoylation branch
pathways.description: HCN + NH3 (+UV) → cyanamide → urea → cyanate; cyanate with ornithine to citrulline → speculative amidination to arginine

pathways.name: Ornithine direct guanidinylation branch
pathways.description: HCN (polymerization/hydrolysis) → ornithine; guanidinylation with cyanamide to arginine

pathways.name: Carbamoylation of ornithine to citrulline, then amidination
pathways.description: HCN → ornithine → citrulline (cyanate carbamoylation) → amidination with cyanamide to arginine

pathways.name: Ornithine guanidinylation via guanidine
pathways.description: HCN + NH3 photolysis → guanidine; guanidine reacts with ornithine to yield arginine (as by analogy to cyanamide pathway)

pathways.name: Ornithine from HCN polymer, urea/cyanate branch
pathways.description: HCN → urea/cyanate via photolysis; carbamoylation and modification of ornithine to arginine via citrulline

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic route with surplus cyanamide from photolysis
pathways.description: HCN + NH3 photolysis to cyanamide and guanidine, both feeding into guanidinylation of aminopropionitrile or ornithine depending on pool composition.

pathways.name: Ornithine → arginine via speculative citrulline amidination and parallel guanidinylation
pathways.description: Ornithine from HCN polymer + cyanamide: can go via guanidinylation (rxn_010) or carbamoylation → citrulline → amidination (rxn_011, rxn_014); alternate functionalization routes.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the most literature-aligned pathway (cyanosulfidic, per Patel et al. 2015), but suffers from multiple mass balance violations (rxn_002, rxn_003, rxn_006). The sequence from HCN/acetylene to acrylonitrile and then β-aminopropionitrile is chemically plausible, but several steps (notably guanidinylation and homologation) are unbalanced and cannot be mass-conserved with small species. The final hydrolysis to arginine (rxn_007) is speculative (not demonstrated), correctly annotated as speculative, but also unchecked for balance. These errors lower chemical feasibility and target achievement. Environmental progression is soundly implemented (surface/UV photochemistry), matching the cited environment. Approval not possible due to balance errors.
suggestions: Explicitly balance all reactions by identifying missing small molecules (e.g., H2 or HCN, as suggested by mass differences).
For rxn_007, specify whether the reaction is literally plausible or intended as an annotated formal hydrolysis.
Ensure stated intermediates have unambiguous, balanceable formulas and names.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This branch introduces photoreduction to access β-aminopropionaldehyde, but its key steps (rxn_002, rxn_003, rxn_004, rxn_006) all fail atom conservation. Rxn_004 (reduction of β-aminopropionitrile to aldehyde) cannot be balanced; reaction pathway is unclear. Pathway is chemically plausible in concept but not as written. Environmental consistency holds (all plausible surface photochemistry). Target achievement is low due to these issues.
suggestions: Correct all mass/charge imbalances; clarify small-molecule loss/gain.
Redefine ambiguous or unparsed molecules for clearer mass tracking.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This route relies on photolytically generated cyanamide to accelerate cyanosulfidic extension. All issues above recur: major steps unbalanced, ambiguous mass/water/hydrogen sources, and speculative final step. Still, this is one of the best-supported prebiotic branches mechanistically. Environmental context well matched (surface UV, as per Patel).
suggestions: Explicitly balance rxn_008; ensure hydrogen flow is tracked.
Update immediate intermediates’ formulas to resolve structure parsing and mass mismatches.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This ‘carbamoylation branch’ with urea/cyanate and citrulline intermediates represents a plausible biosynthetic-mimicking route. However, rxn_011 is unbalanced (C, H, N, O all off); rxn_014 is plausible but speculative. The final conversion (citrulline to arginine by cyanamide amidination) is not supported by experiment, only by chemical analogy. Environmental progression well handled.
suggestions: Balance the citrulline-forming and amidination reactions (rxn_011, rxn_014); check for possible missing small byproducts such as CO2.
Explicitly state that the citrulline→arginine step is theoretical.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Direct guanidinylation of ornithine represents the ornithine-centric route supported by literature for peptide/protein-bound ornithine only (Longo et al. 2020). However, rxn_009 is unbalanced by multiple elements (C, H, N, O); ornithine formation from HCN is literature-attributed, but in reality only shown with disputed methodology. The guanidinylation step (rxn_010) is plausible but unproven for the free monomer under prebiotic conditions.
suggestions: Explicitly annotate the uncertainty in free ornithine guanidinylation.
Check balance for rxn_009 and adjust small-molecule byproducts.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Ornithine → citrulline → arginine via cyanate and cyanamide is a theoretical biosynthetic mimic, but both key steps (rxn_009 and rxn_011) are unbalanced. Final amidination to arginine (rxn_014) is plausible in synthetic chemistry but unverified and speculative in prebiotic context.
suggestions: Annotate this pathway as speculative, given absence of experimental arginine formation.
Fix atom/charge budget for biosynthetic-mimic steps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Ornithine guanidinylation via guanidine is chemically plausible but not prebiotically demonstrated for the free amino acid (see Longo et al. 2020). The upstream HCN → ornithine step (rxn_009) is unbalanced and not replicated experimentally. Guanidine availability is supported (HCN photolysis); free-base guanidinylation of ornithine is speculative.
suggestions: Correct mass balance in HCN polymerization.
Explicitly state speculative status for free-ornithine guanidinylation.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Mixes cyanosulfidic and HCN-polymer pathways to reach ornithine, urea/cyanate, and citrulline/arginine. Stepwise logic is consistent, but several steps are unbalanced or ambiguous, notably rxn_002, rxn_003, rxn_009, and rxn_011. Final step (rxn_014) is speculative, as above.
suggestions: Balance all polymer/hydrolysis/intermediate reactions.
Clarify fate of hydrogens, ammonias, and other small species in redox and hydrolysis steps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: A streamlined cyanosulfidic branch with surplus cyanamide, this pathway benefits from potential for higher yields, but repeats unbalanced steps with the same structural ambiguities as in P1/P3. Literature alignment is reasonable up to the arginine α-aminonitrile level, but not beyond due to missing or unverified hydrolysis.
suggestions: Ensure all steps are atom/charge balanced with explicit byproducts.
If any intermediates are not parseable, check SMILES/InChI or redefine as needed.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Combines multiple ornithine → arginine routes, clearly reflecting known gaps: HCN polymer/ornithine yield is unverified (rxn_009 unbalanced), citrulline → arginine step is speculative. Good pathway logic but hampered by chemical and mass-balance errors.
suggestions: Re-specify ambiguous or unparseable intermediates.
Explicitly annotate speculative reaction steps.

evaluation.network_feedback: This network represents an impressively comprehensive and literature-aligned attempt to model all currently evidenced and plausible prebiotic arginine synthesis routes, incorporating appropriate environmental and mechanistic diversity. Nonetheless, the network as specified fails at the level of chemical feasibility and mass conservation: the majority of key reactions are not atom/charge balanced as written, per the deterministic check, and several intermediates are structurally ambiguous or unparseable. These issues prevent approval despite the high level of research and strategic pathway construction. Fundamentals such as balance checks, explicit enumeration of byproducts, and clarity of molecular identities must be addressed before the network can be validated. All literature claims, especially those relating to ornithine guanidinylation and the cyanosulfidic network, are properly cited and caveated. Target achievement scores are penalized due to absence of an experimentally validated final hydrolysis to arginine proper in any branch. Environmental consistency and pathway logic are exemplary. Correcting the above balance and specification errors would bring the network to approval standard.
